definition: Commerce in which AI agents participate materially in discovery, decision-making, transaction execution, or post-purchase workflows.
The broader economic layer in which software agents consume services, pay, earn, coordinate, and transact with businesses or other agents.
Informal shorthand for making a business or product legible, trustworthy, retrievable, and actionable to AI agents. Not a single standardized protocol.
A machine-readable document describing a business protocol version, services, and capabilities; UCP commonly publishes this at /.well-known/ucp.
A machine-readable declaration of an agent platform's supported protocol capabilities used during capability negotiation.
Read-only contextual content exposed by an MCP server at a URI.
A callable operation exposed by an MCP server with a structured input schema.
Structured merchant product data delivered to a platform for discovery, listing, advertising, or commerce experiences.
A stable product or variant identifier used as the source identity across downstream catalogs and feeds.
